key_insight: Wearable high-frequency temperature data plus machine learning may help distinguish engraftment fevers from other fever causes in hospitalized HCT patients.
clinical_relevance: If validated, this approach could support faster fever triage and reduce diagnostic uncertainty during febrile neutropenia in stem cell transplant care.
method: 68 fever episodes from 90 HCT patients were monitored with an FDA-cleared wearable temperature sensor every 2 minutes.
Temperature features from 1 hour before to 3 hours after fever onset were used to train machine-learning classifiers.
Repeated stratified 5-fold patient-level cross-validation compared models for classifying engraftment fever vs other etiologies.
evidence_signal: Logistic regression performed best, with 94% specificity and mean AUROC 0.88 across 100 train-test evaluations.
watch_item: This is a small, single-setting retrospective study, so real-world performance and generalizability still need prospective validation.
paper_title: Rapid diagnosis of fever etiology using wearable temperature monitoring and machine learning
